**Finding: WARRANTY — compliant (no redline proposed).**

Section 19 meets the preferred position, not merely the fallback:

| Element | Where satisfied |
|---|---|
| Professional and workmanlike | §19.1 — plus qualified personnel and industry standards |
| Conformity to documentation | §19.1 (Services and Deliverables) and §19.2 |
| Software period | §19.2 — hosted Services conform **throughout the subscription term**; with §§8.1–8.2 (three-year term, twelve-month renewals) this equals or beats the preferred 12 months |
| Services/Deliverable period | §19.2 — ninety days from delivery **or acceptance, whichever is later**; §19.1's performance warranty carries no durational cut-off at all |
| Repair / replacement | §19.4 — prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge |
| Refund | §19.4 — termination of the affected item plus refund of Fees paid |
| Compliance with law | §19.3 |
| No malicious code | §19.3 |

Two checks that often defeat this rule both come out in our favour: the disclaimer does **not** swallow the express warranty (§19.5 disclaims implied warranties only and expressly preserves express warranties, service levels, indemnities and remedies), and there is no "AS IS" language anywhere in the document. §19.4 also keeps the remedy non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims, reinforced by §§9.5 and 30.2.

Noted in the rationale rather than flagged as deviations: the no-malicious-code warranty reaches only code "intentionally introduced by Vendor," and the refund arises after Vendor fails to cure within a reasonable period rather than at our election. Neither is material, and the clause runs in our favour, so I have left it untouched.
